title: Traffic circuit-breakers and safety thresholds for gradual upgrades
creator: Samantha Ortiz
description:
Problem: We need a robust, predictable mechanism to run gradual upgrades of runtime components and model variants across hosted and Dedicated pools. Current canary tooling ramps traffic but lacks clear circuit-breaker semantics and automatic safe-pausing when regressions appear. That gap causes extended incidents and manual intervention for rollbacks.

Goal: Implement traffic circuit-breakers and safety thresholds that automatically pause or scale back rollouts when key health signals degrade. The system should be policy-driven, observable in Console, and compatible with feature-flag based gating and existing percentage ramp flows. It must work for both short-lived canaries (minutes) and longer progressive ramps (hours/days).

Scope: Implement server-side gating logic in the routing/orchestration layer and Console controls for policy configuration and real-time status. Build a small state machine that drives ramp steps, evaluates metrics, triggers pause/rollback, and emits audit events. Provide a simulation mode and a replay tool to validate policies against historical traffic/metrics. Exclude deep UI redesign; Console changes can be lightweight (policy editor + status view).

Non-goals: Not handling cross-region capacity rewrites or per-customer custom SLOs beyond threshold overrides. Storage of long-term audit history will be limited to 90 days in this Iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Routing layer enforces a policy that pauses or reduces ramp when thresholds are exceeded for configured windows
Default safety policy shipped: error_rate > 1.5% over 5m OR p95 latency > 25% above baseline over 5m triggers a pause
Console shows active rollout state, last triggered reason, and permits manual resume/rollback
Automated rollback path exists: if policy violation persists for 15 minutes after pause, system can optionally rollback to previous stable variant
Simulation mode can run a policy against a stored 24h traffic slice and produce a report with hypothetical triggers
E2E tests (integration + chaos) demonstrate that a noisy canary is paused within 2 evaluation windows
Audit events for each gate transition are emitted to the observability pipeline with trace IDs and responsible actor

design_notes: State machine: IDLE -> RAMPING -> PAUSED -> VERIFY -> ROLLBACK/COMPLETED. PAUSED can transition to ROLL-FORWARD after manual resume or automatic stabilize detection
Evaluation window: rolling 5m window by default, configurable per-policy. Use sliding windows computed from existing PromQL-like pipeline
Metrics for triggers: request_error_rate (5xx+client-side loss), p95_latency, tail_tokens_per_request (for cost regressions), model-quality-signal (when available)
Threshold semantics: absolute and relative thresholds. Example default: p95 > baseline * 1.25 AND delta > 50ms to avoid small noise triggering
Ramp strategy: staged percentage sequence with backoff. Default sequence: 0.5%, 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%. Backoff policy doubles wait time on each detected instability

Rollback: two modes - soft pause (stops ramp) and hard rollback (switch traffic back). Hard rollback requires either (a) persistent violation for configured duration or (b) explicit policy that allows auto-rollback
Audit and trace: each decision logs a structured event with (policy_id, reason, metrics_snapshot, trace_id, actor). Events written to observability topic and Console timeline
Simulation: deterministic replay uses sampled traces and metric streams; we capture decisions and produce a sensitivity report showing which thresholds triggered
risks_and_mitigation: False positives: overly aggressive thresholds can pause healthy rollouts. Mitigation: require both relative and absolute delta for latency triggers, and provide a staging simulation to tune policies
Delayed signal: important regressions may only appear after user-profiled workloads. Mitigation: include cost/quality signals and longer watch windows for high-risk models
Operational complexity: many policies could confuse SREs. Mitigation: ship sane defaults, a small policy library, and UI affordances to preview policy effect
Cross-service interaction: rollout policy could interact poorly with autoscaling/backfill. Mitigation: explicitly document interactions and add guardrail to ignore internal autoscaler probe failures
Performance impact: evaluation must be low-latency. Mitigation: run evaluation in routing control plane using pre-aggregated metrics streams, not per-request checks
